validity.recommendation: ref-fill Status/Fuel/PipelineType/FuelSource/Location/Owner as below; correct EndLocation spelling 'Ramgahr' -> 'Ramgarh'; leave StartYearEarliest blank pending resolution of a real date conflict across sources (see notes)
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/ATTRIBUTION confirmed via sources genuinely independent of GEM. Indus Gas Limited's own operations page (www.indusgas.com/operation.php -- Indus holds 63-90% of the RJ-ON/6 block over time, financing the SGL field) states: 'Within a short period of one year a large infrastructure development consisting of a dedicated 6" gas pipeline of ca. 90 km (owned by GAIL) connecting SGL Field with an existing power generation unit ... were completed and commercial sale of gas commenced ... GAIL has entered into a back to back gas sale arrangement with a 270 MW Rajasthan State owned power plant located at Ramgarh.' Business Standard (independent news outlet, 2009-08-07) reports: 'GAIL (India) Limited has signed a Gas Sales and Transmission Contract (GSTC) with Rajasthan Rajya Vidyut Utpadan Nigam Limited (RRVUNL) for supply of natural gas for 160 MW gas power plant of RRVUNL at Ramgarh. GAIL also signed a Gas Sales and Purchase Agreement (GSPA) with the SGL consortium -- the contractors of RJ-ON/6 block.' Two NS Energy Business trade-press articles corroborate and add detail: the GSTC-signing piece states the pipeline is '90 kilometers long', '10 inch diameter', connects 'the RJ-ON/6 block to RRVUNL's power facility at Ramgarh', is GAIL-owned/constructed ('estimated investment of approximately INR1 billion'), and gas originates from 'the RJ-ON/6 block in Shahgarh, Jaisalmer district' (matches GEM StartState/Province=Rajasthan); the SGL-completion piece (as of June 2010) confirms 'Production facilities and pipeline completed and ready for operation', pipeline length '90 kilometers', operator GAIL, route 'From SGL gas field to Ramgarh power plant'. Together these four independent-origin sources (operator's own site; a national business daily; two syndicated trade-press pieces citing the GAIL/RRVUNL press release) confirm: Status=operating (real, in-service pipeline), Fuel=Gas, PipelineType=transmission (a dedicated field-to-single-consumer transmission line -- not a gathering line, since it runs well outside the field boundary to an external power-plant offtaker, and not distribution; correctly classified per GEM's three-way PipelineType vocabulary), FuelSource=SGL Field (the SGL discovery/field within block RJ-ON/6), Owner=GAIL (India) Ltd 100% (GAIL built, owns and operates the line; RRVUNL/RJ-ON-6 consortium are the gas buyer/seller, not pipeline owners), StartLocation=Langtala and EndState/Province=Rajasthan. One correction: GEM's EndLocation 'Ramgahr' is a misspelling of 'Ramgarh' (the town/power-plant name is consistently spelled 'Ramgarh' across all four sources) -- recommend a sheet-side spelling fix, not a value change. DUPLICATE CHECK against the 35-row India roster: P1436 and P3905 (Dandewala-Gamnewala-RSEB Ramgarh Gas Pipeline) both terminate at the same Ramgarh power plant, raising a relabel/double-count question. Resolved as NOT a duplicate: independent reporting (infrastructuretoday.co.in, 2026, on a related ONGC Chinnewala Tibba announcement) confirms 'ONGC, OIL and Focus Energy Ltd. are among the gas suppliers to the [Ramgarh] plant' and that 'ONGC commenced gas evacuation to RRVUNL's Ramgarh power plant via its Gamnewala Gas Collection Station' -- i.e. Ramgarh receives gas from multiple, physically distinct dedicated pipelines from different fields/producers. P3905 draws from ONGC's Gamnewala and OIL's Dandewala fields (PNGRB-authorised 2012-12-14, ~65 km), while P1436 draws from Focus Energy/Indus Gas's SGL field via Langtala (~90 km, no PNGRB common-carrier itemisation found because it is a dedicated, not common-carrier, line -- consistent with the country guidance that dedicated/tie-in lines sit inside PNGRB's grand totals but are not itemised; confirmed by fetching the current PNGRB register, https://pngrb.gov.in/data-bank/20260531-NGPL-MIS-Report.pdf, and finding no 'Ramgarh'/'Langtala'/'SGL'/'Focus Energy' row). Different upstream fields, different producers, different lengths, different authorisation status -- two real, separate pipelines feeding one plant, not a duplicate. UNRESOLVED CAVEAT -- commissioning date: sources disagree on when the pipeline itself entered service. Indus Gas's own summary page implies the dedicated pipeline was complete and commercial gas sale began July 2009 ('within a short period of one year' of the March 2009 SGL Field Development approval). But both NS Energy Business articles (one covering the Aug-2009 GSTC signing, one dated to facility completion) instead point to construction completing Feb-Jun 2010 and full commercial gas supply beginning April-July 2010, with full capacity reached April 2011. Given this genuine conflict between an operator's own retrospective marketing copy and two independent trade-press pieces with more specific dated milestones, I did not fill StartYearEarliest -- flagging for Update to resolve (most likely 2009 was an early/interim gas sale before the dedicated GAIL pipeline itself was finished in 2010, but that is inference, not confirmed).

validity.recommendation: correct Capacity from 0.12 to approximately 0.95 MMSCMD (and recompute CapacityBcm/y / CapacityBOEd accordingly) -- the sheet value looks stale/wrong by roughly a factor of 8
validity.researcher_notes: SPEC check on Capacity. GEM has Capacity=0.12 MMSCMD (CapacityBcm/y=0.04). Two independent sources materially disagree: Indus Gas's own site states GAIL committed to a gas off-take of 'around 33.5 mmcf/d (processed gas) under "Take or Pay" terms' under the August 2009 GSPA -- converting, 33.5 MMSCFD x 0.0283168 m3/ft3 = ~0.949 MMSCMD. NS Energy Business's GSTC article independently states the same contract explicitly in metric terms: the pipeline 'will transport 0.95 MMSCMD of natural gas for a period of 12 years.' These two independent-origin sources (company disclosure; trade press citing the GAIL/RRVUNL press release) agree with each other to three significant figures (~0.95 MMSCMD) and both conflict sharply with the sheet's 0.12 MMSCMD -- roughly an 8x gap, far beyond rounding or unit-confusion. I could not find any source supporting 0.12 MMSCMD specifically (not even the field's early, modest 7 mmcf/d = ~0.20 MMSCMD startup flow in July 2009 matches it). This does not fit the country-wide 'CapacityBcm/y derived from PNGRB's authorised MMSCMD' pattern either, since this dedicated line is not itemised in PNGRB's common-carrier register at all (confirmed against the current 2026-05-31 edition), so there is no obvious stale-authorisation explanation for where 0.12 came from -- most likely a straightforward data error. Flagging as a concern rather than a direct fill because Capacity is not blank on the sheet (an existing value should be corrected via Update, not silently overwritten by a ref-sweep fill).

validity.recommendation: correct LengthKnown from 88.00 to 90.00 km -- three independent mentions consistently give 90 km
validity.researcher_notes: SPEC check on Length. GEM has LengthKnown=88.00 km (LengthMergedKm=88.00, RouteAccuracy=low). Three independent-origin sources give 90 km: Indus Gas's own site ('a dedicated 6" gas pipeline of ca. 90 km'), NS Energy Business's GSTC article ('90 kilometers long'), and NS Energy Business's SGL-completion article ('Length: 90 kilometers'). No source found supporting exactly 88 km. The gap is modest (~2.3%, 2 km) and RouteAccuracy is already flagged 'low' on the sheet, so this is a minor rather than severe discrepancy, but three consistent, precise citations against one unsourced sheet figure is enough to flag rather than silently pass -- especially since GEM's own LengthEstimateKm=93.06 (a geometry-derived estimate) is closer to the sourced 90 km than the sheet's stated LengthKnown=88.00 is.
